thread:
maria_acme: Hey team, ACME is reporting a sharp P99 increase for requests from APAC since 09:10 UTC. They say traces show a hop into us-west-2 before hitting our inference nodes. Can we confirm if any fallbacks or egress changes happened?

sara_support: Sorry to hear that — can you paste one of the trace IDs or a short span dump? Also which model/route are they using?

maria_acme: Model: open-rw-7b, route: /v1/generate (prod). Trace ID: trace-2026-03-17-0912-AB12. Sample curl they used: `curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer <redacted>\" https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate -d '{"model":"open-rw-7b","prompt":"hi"}'`

trace-bot: (automated) Ingested trace trace-2026-03-17-0912-AB12 -> spans: client->edge-ap-sg->egress-proxy->us-west-2-proxy->inference-us-west-2->inference-us-west-2

alex_ops: Hmm that trace shows an actual egress hop to us-west-2. No deploys in the last 6h on routing services. @kumar_sre can you check smart-routing config and capacity shards for ap-sg region?

kumar_sre: Looking. Smart-routing policy for ACME account is `region_preference: [ap-sg, ap-sin, us-west-2]` with `fallback: enabled`. Current capacity in ap-sg GPU pool is 0 available (reserved jobs) at 09:05-09:20 UTC. Autoscaler did not spin up because burst_quota was exhausted. So requests got routed to next fallback which is us-west-2.

sara_support: That explains the hop, but why did the trace show an extra `egress-proxy` before the us-west hop? Any intermediate NAT/peering change?

jordan_net: We had a scheduled peering maintenance earlier this week but no config pushed today. The egress proxy logs show `OUTBOUND: selected-egress-cluster: us-west-2-fallback` for that trace id. Looks like route decision happened at edge due to capacity check.

maria_acme: The problem is client expects APAC latency. This cross-region hop adds ~250ms and causes user timeouts, plus billing spike. Any urgent mitigation?

alex_ops: Short-term mitigations: 1) force route by header: clients can set `X-Region: ap-sg` to prefer local edge (we already accept it for debugging), 2) temporarily expand burst_quota for ACME team from the console, 3) enable another apac pod pool (if fast). Which do you want us to try?

maria_acme: Can you try expanding burst_quota first and re-run a test? Also we'll set X-Region for repro.

kumar_sre: Done — increased burst_quota by 30% at 09:30 UTC for the account. I also kicked a manual scale on ap-sg pool.

trace-bot: (automated) New trace trace-2026-03-17-0935-CD34 -> spans: client->edge-ap-sg->inference-ap-sg-1 -> inference-ap-sg-1. P99 reduced from 820ms -> 110ms.

sara_support: Nice. Maria, can you confirm ACME sees improved latency and whether any billing anomalies persist?

maria_acme: Verified — latency back to expected. Billing: they see a one-off extra egress unit billed due to the earlier us-west routing. They're asking for credit for those spikes.

alex_ops: For the billing ask, route-related cross-region egress is covered by our incident credits policy. I'll file a request to finance with the trace IDs and times. @maria_acme please add the customer billing contact so we can loop them in.

maria_acme: Added billing contact. Thanks. A couple notes for follow-up: - can we add a routing alert when regional GPU pool available capacity drops below 10% for high-traffic accounts? - also want a knob to prefer strict-region-routing (reject vs fallback) per account.

kumar_sre: Ack. I'll open an RFC for an alert (alert: regional_pool_free_pct < 10% for 3m) and an account-level `strict_region` flag we can wire into the router. Also adding a preflight check in autoscaler to log burst_quota exhaustion events.

sara_support: Closing loop: customer satisfied for now. Documenting steps: 1) identified fallback due to exhausted burst_quota & empty ap-sg pool, 2) increased burst_quota + manual scale, 3) confirmed traces and P99 improvement, 4) finance ticket for one-off credit.

maria_acme: Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

alex_ops: Follow-ups assigned to Kumar (RFC + alert) and Alex (finance ticket). Marking thread resolved. :white_check_mark:
